reflections.summary: Won 2-0. The main reason was the successful opening: Prankster Tailwind let Kingambit immediately remove Mega Gengar, then Whimsicott and Kingambit eliminated Meowscarada before Whimsicott fell. Gyarados's Intimidate and Taunt disrupted Toxapex, while repeated Kingambit pressure eventually removed the defensive core and Pelipper. The chosen four suited this matchup, and the sets performed their intended jobs: Focus Sash Whimsicott supplied speed control, Black Glasses Kingambit provided decisive Dark/Steel pressure, and Taunt Gyarados was useful against Toxapex. Passimian contributed only at the finish, so its slot was less important. No between-game adjustment is documented in the supplied evidence; therefore it cannot be credited or blamed, but the game-two plan clearly succeeded. Not evolving a Mega was acceptable because the non-Mega Kingambit/Gyarados core immediately answered the opponent's Mega Gengar.
reflections.adjustment: Against a future rematch, preserve the same priority of removing Mega Gengar immediately and using Tailwind plus Dark/Steel pressure. Consider whether Passimian is necessary in the four, since it saw almost no meaningful action; Gholdengo or Hatterene could be tested if their prepared sets offer a stronger answer to the opponent's status or defensive play, though the evidence does not prove either is better. Keep Gyarados available for Intimidate and Taunt, but respect rain-boosted Surf and Pelipper's Hurricane; its Wacan Berry did not address Hurricane, and the critical hit nearly removed it. Do not expose Gholdengo before Mega Gengar is handled. The registered six were broadly sensible, while Volcarona and Gliscor are less appealing into rain and Pelipper; there is no supplied evidence that Aromatisse or Meowstic-Female would improve this matchup. The preparation correctly identified Gyarados, Kingambit, and Whimsicott's utility, but could improve the fourth-slot plan and direct counterplay to rain and Hurricane.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Mega Gengar with strong special coverage including Shadow Ball, Sludge Wave, Thunderbolt, and Focus Blast; removing it early is a priority. Pelipper carries Drizzle, Damp Rock, Hurricane, Surf, U-turn, and Roost: expect extended rain, pivoting, and strong Flying pressure, especially against Whimsicott and Gyarados. Toxapex carries Leftovers, Recover, Baneful Bunker, Toxic Spikes, and Surf; Taunt is valuable, and it can be worn down by focused physical pressure. Meowscarada is Life Orb Protean with Dark Pulse, Energy Ball, Leaf Storm, and U-turn; do not give it free turns after a switch-in. Unbrought Garchomp is Choice Scarf and can be locked into Fire Fang after selection. Unbrought Clefable carries Light Clay screens, Thunder Wave, and Moonblast. Preserve Gyarados for Intimidate and Ice Fang utility, maintain Dark/Steel pressure, and avoid exposing Gholdengo until Mega Gengar is handled. Whimsicott's Focus Sash, Prankster Tailwind, and Moonblast are effective tempo tools; Kingambit's Defiant, Black Glasses, and immediate attacks are central to the matchup. Reconsider Passimian as the fourth bring and prepare a clearer answer to rain-boosted attacks and Pelipper's Hurricane.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 in a series where team preparation failed to match the opponent's Whimsicott/Kingambit/Gyarados physical offense core. In game 2, Mega Gengar was KO'd turn 1 by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave (Fighting super effective vs Ghost) providing zero value. Meowscarada was KO'd turn 2 by the Whimsicott+Kingambit double-targeting combination. Toxapex was Taunt-locked by Gyarados and never set Toxic Spikes or contributed meaningfully, then got overwhelmed by the physical duo. Pelipper was the only functional Pokémon — it removed Whimsicott, survived multiple hits, and critically damaged Gyarados to 16% via Hurricane — but one Pokémon cannot carry a 6v6. Clefable never entered. Passimian entered only at turn 7 with the game already lost. The core problem: no Fighting-resistant or Intimidate-bearing Pokémon in the active four, leaving Kingambit completely unchecked. Decision-making was clean (0 errors), but the roster construction was the loss.
reflections.adjustment: 1) Reconsider Mega Gengar as a pick against any team that may run Kingambit or strong Fighting coverage — it is a dead pick that provides zero defensive utility. 2) Swap in Skarmory or Scrafty (both left behind) for one of the fragile offensive picks: Skarmory walls Fighting moves, sets Spikes/Whirlwind, and pivots with U-turn; Scrafty intimidates and threatens Kingambit with Dark STAB. 3) Do not rely on a single Taunt-vulnerable Pokémon (Toxapex) for all hazard-setting; spread hazard options or bring a Prankster user. 4) Against rain-boosted physical cores with Intimidate support, ensure at least one lead that can absorb Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head and retaliate. 5) Re-evaluate bringing Clefable over one of the glassier picks — its utility (Magic Bounce, Encore, bulk) could have broken the Taunt/Hazard stall loop.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core pattern: Whimsicott Tailwind + Focus Sash sets speed control for Kingambit/Passimian physical sweep. Kingambit Adamant BlackGlasses Kowtow Cleave is devastating vs neutral or weak targets — Intimidate from Gyarados softens physical walls further. Gyarados WacanBerry + Intimidate + Taunt is a defensive pivot that cripples setup and physical attackers. Passimian ExpertBelt CloseCombat is a strong finisher at full HP. Opponent reserves: Gholdengo (MakeItRain, Shadow Ball, Thunderbolt, Life Orb, Good-as-Gold) — immune to status, hits hard specially; Hatterene (Trick Room, ExpandingForce, DazzlingGleam, Mental Herb) — potential Trick Room reverser. Durable takeaways: Kingambit punishes stat-drop strategies — avoid Intimidate/stat-move sequences into its Kowtow Cleave. Taunt shuts Toxapex's entire gameplan. Tailwind turns speed tiers against slower pivots. Rain benefits the opponent's Gyarados Waterfall more than it helps if the offensive core is physical. Next time: bring Fighting resistance, spread hazard-setting, and avoid two fragile sweepers in the same four.
